comparisons.peer_summary: In fiscal year 2024, the company's global voluntary attrition rate was approximately 2.9% (excluding VMware merger employees) and 6.2% (including them), both below the technology industry benchmark from AON's 2024 study.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Broadcom disclose specific voluntary/overall turnover rates for fiscal year 2024 to measure employee retention, a key aspect of human capital management. NVIDIA reported an overall turnover rate of 2.7%, while Broadcom reported a global voluntary attrition rate of 2.9% (excluding VMware merger employees) and 6.2% (including them), both benchmarked against industry standards. While Broadcom provides a more detailed breakdown by merger impact and industry comparison, both companies use these low single-digit percentages to demonstrate successful retention efforts in a competitive talent market.

sentences.text: In fiscal year 2024, our overall turnover rate was 2.7%.

Our global voluntary attrition rates in fiscal year 2024 were approximately 2.9% (excluding employees who joined Broadcom as a result of the VMware Merger) and approximately 6.2% (including employees who joined Broadcom as a result of the VMware Merger), which are both below the technology industry benchmark (AON, 2024 Salary Increase and Turnover Study - Second Edition, September 2024).

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces significant competition for talent and limited hiring in 2024, with headcount actions expected to decrease the core workforce by approximately 15% by early 2025. Undesired turnover rates were 5.9% in 2024 and 5.6% in 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Intel disclose their undesired or overall turnover rates for fiscal year 2024, though the metrics and contexts differ significantly. NVIDIA reported a very low overall turnover rate of 2.7%, reflecting a stable workforce where employees 'tend to come and stay.' In contrast, Intel reported an 'undesired turnover rate' of 5.9% in 2024, contextualized by significant headcount reductions (15% decrease expected) and limited hiring due to a restructuring plan, indicating higher involuntary or performance-driven departures compared to NVIDIA's retention-focused narrative.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of September 29, 2024, Qualcomm had approximately 49,000 employees (mostly full-time) representing over 100 nationalities across 150 locations in 37 countries, with a voluntary turnover rate of approximately 5% in fiscal 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Qualcomm report voluntary turnover rates for fiscal year 2024 as a measure of workforce stability. NVIDIA reported an overall turnover rate of 2.7%, while Qualcomm reported a voluntary turnover rate of approximately 5%. Both disclosures highlight low attrition relative to broader industry norms, though Qualcomm provides additional demographic context (global workforce size and nationalities) alongside the turnover metric, whereas NVIDIA focuses on the retention philosophy of long-term career building.
